title: Open a casement window wide on its peg stay, to the last hole
instruction: Open the window as wide as its stay allows, with the stay's last hole on the pin, and let go.
context: Societal relatability: anyone who airs a room with a side-hung timber or steel casement window. Such windows are held open by a peg stay, the standard fitting sold for them: a bar hinged on the sash with a row of holes, dropped over a pin on the window board; the hole that sits on the pin sets how far the window stays open. The window here rests on its first open hole and is to be opened as wide as it goes. Pushed along without being carried, the bar drops into the next hole it passes and the window opens only a little; let go off a hole, the sash is free to swing and slam. The bar has to be lifted, carried clear over the nearer hole while the sash swings out under it, then set on the pin so the last hole drops over it.
setup: Station table; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Window board, fixed: 290 x 488 mm, its top 40 mm up, from x 22.0 to 51.0 cm, centred on y 0. (2) Casement window, 488 x 600 mm overall, standing on the board across the table; jambs and head 45 mm wide, 70 mm deep. Its sash (396 x 509 mm, 44 mm thick, painted timber with a 4 mm pane: 3.1 kg) is hinged on the robot's left (+y) at its outside face, x 46.4 cm, y +19.8 cm, and opens outward, away from the robot; its room face is at x 42.0 cm when shut. Its fastener is undone. (3) A brass peg stay, Samuel Heath P4512-B (254 mm series, 278.6 mm overall), on the sash's bottom rail: its swivel 11.1 mm in front of the sash, 139 mm right of the window's centre line when shut; the bar (13.6 mm wide, 8 mm deep, an 8.1 mm groove along its underside) lifts on a pin 20 mm from the swivel. Four holes 7.2 mm across, 64.5, 105.0, 145.5 and 186.0 mm from the swivel; a curled tail ends in a 14 mm ball 260.5 mm from the swivel. (4) Two brass pins as supplied, on the board at x 40.9 cm: A at y -7.4 cm, B at y +4.7 cm (under holes 1 and 4 when shut). Each is a 40 x 15 mm plate and a taper 22.5 mm tall, 7.9 mm across at its foot and 5.6 mm near its top. Start: the window open 13.5 degrees on its first open hole: hole 2 on pin A, the bar level, its ball at x 29.0 cm, y +2.6 cm, 63 mm above the table. Hole 3 on pin A holds the sash at 22.4 degrees and hole 4 (the last) at 30.8 degrees. Both grippers start open, at least 200 mm from the stay. Run limit 800 steps (40 s).
scoring: Read at the end of the run. A hole is on the pin when its centre is within 2.0 mm of pin A's axis in plan and the pin's tip reaches the bar's top face or stands above it (a straightedge laid on the bar touches the pin). Holes are numbered from the swivel; hole 4 is the last. Let go: the fingers of both grippers 30 mm or more from the stay. Still: over the last second (20 steps) the ball and the sash's free bottom corner moved 1 mm or less. 1.0: hole 4 on pin A, let go on each of the last 20 steps, and still. 0.5: hole 3 on pin A, let go (one setting wider than at the start). 0.25: hole 3 or 4 on pin A while a gripper still holds or touches the stay, or before it is still. 0: anything else: hole 2 still on the pin (the start), the window shut, the stay off the pin (resting on its top or on the board: the sash is free to swing). A hand that enters the space of the glass pane (inside the sash's stiles and rails) scores 0 for the rest of the run: it would strike the glass. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial: look from above for the pin through the hole and lay a straightedge on the bar; then a 5 N push and pull with a spring balance at the sash's free edge must not move it more than the pin's play.
fidelity: Stay and pins at real size from the maker's CAD model. Window size, timber and glass masses, hinge friction (0.2 N m) and where the pins sit are estimates. The pane has no collider (no transparency in the simulator); its mass is in the rails. The ball is a 14 mm disc across the bar, the pins' tapers 16 flat staves. The 5 N tug of the bench check is not applied in simulation: the scorer reads the capture it tests. Nothing is moved or latched by code.
reset_notes: Lift the stay, close the sash to 13.5 degrees open and lower the stay so its second hole drops over pin A, the bar level. Check that the sash swings freely with the stay lifted, that both pins stand upright and that the fastener is undone. Park both grippers open, 200 mm or more from the stay. Nothing is consumed.
